```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
```

Follows `mcda/MCDA_paper_results_spec.md`.

**Hypothesis.** Citizen weights change the priority map less where burdens coincide in space
(Klagenfurt) than where they are decoupled (Malta).

**Analyses.**

- **A. Burden coincidence:** Spearman correlation matrix of the normalised criteria, mean absolute correlation, PCA (share of variance of the first component), share of scored cells in the top quintile of three or more criteria.
- **B. Sensitivity to weights in general:** 1,000 random weight sets drawn uniformly over the weight simplex (Dirichlet, all parameters 1, fixed seed), each compared with the equal weights score.
- **C. Controls:** (1) B with the five criteria shared by both cities; (2) map change per unit of weight change, citizen vs equal weights.
- **D. Robust and contested cells:** per cell, the share of the 1,000 draws in which it is in the top quintile.
- **Leave one out and Table S6:** computed in the two scoring notebooks, shown here.

**Rules.**

- Inputs are the current saved scores.
- Cells are the scored set of the main score: eligible cells, available weight rule (at least 80% of the weight). Every alternative weighting is computed on the same cells, as the scoring notebooks do for equal weights.
- The score is the weighted mean over the available criteria.
- Spearman only.
- Klagenfurt has one row per `ID`.
- Criteria are counted at the criterion level. Klagenfurt air quality is the mean of the available NO2 and PM2.5 indicators (spec 3.2), so Klagenfurt has 6 criteria with equal weight 1/6 (spec 2.3). Its citizen weight is the sum of the two half weights.

```{r libraries}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

OUT <- here::here("output/figures_mcda/burden_coincidence_2026_11_20")
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
SEED    <- 20261120
N_DRAWS <- 1000
N_PERM  <- 200
city_cols <- c(Malta = "#2166ac", Klagenfurt = "#b2182b")
# Tables: formatted HTML when knitting; a plain printed table when a chunk is run interactively
# (kableExtra HTML shows as raw code in the editor)
knitting <- function() isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))
ktab <- function(x, caption, digits = 3) {
  x <- x %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(., digits)))
  if (!knitting()) {
    cat("\n", caption, "\n", sep = "")
    print(as.data.frame(x), row.names = FALSE)
    return(invisible(x))
  }
  x %>% kable(caption = caption) %>% kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
}
```

# Inputs and weights

```{r inputs}
malta <- readRDS(here::here("data/malta/malta_mcda_processed_realloc.rds"))
klag  <- readRDS(here::here("data/klagenfurt/klagenfurt_mcda_priority_may.rds"))
stopifnot(nrow(malta) == 10657, n_distinct(malta$gid) == 10657,
          nrow(klag) == 12418, n_distinct(klag$ID) == 12418)
# Provenance of the scores read (added 2026-11-25)
score_files <- here::here(c("data/malta/malta_mcda_processed_realloc.rds", "data/klagenfurt/klagenfurt_mcda_priority_may.rds"))
ktab(tibble(file = sub(paste0(here::here(), "/"), "", score_files), md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(score_files)),
            modified = format(file.mtime(score_files), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), read_at = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")),
     "Score files read by this notebook")

# Citizen weights recovered exactly from the saved score (weighted sum on cells with all criteria)
recover_weights <- function(df, vars, score = "priority_citizen") {
  d <- st_drop_geometry(df)
  cc <- d[complete.cases(d[, vars]) & !is.na(d[[score]]), ]
  fit <- lm(reformulate(vars, score, intercept = FALSE), data = cc)
  stopifnot(max(abs(residuals(fit))) < 1e-8, abs(sum(coef(fit)) - 1) < 1e-8)
  coef(fit)
}

m_vars <- c("norm_lst", "norm_imd", "norm_dist_bs", "norm_Lden", "norm_traffic", "norm_no2", "norm_tree",
            "norm_green_time", "norm_dist_rec", "norm_green_exp")
m_lab  <- c("Urban heat", "Grey infrastructure", "Blue space", "Noise", "Traffic", "Air quality",
            "Street greenery", "Green proximity", "Recreation", "Green per person")
m_w <- recover_weights(malta, m_vars)[m_vars]

k_ind <- c("norm_lst", "norm_dist_bs", "norm_no2", "norm_pm25", "norm_green_time", "norm_traffic_cat",
           "norm_income_weighted")
k_w7 <- recover_weights(klag, k_ind)[k_ind]
stopifnot(abs(k_w7["norm_no2"] - k_w7["norm_pm25"]) < 1e-10)
klag <- klag %>% mutate(norm_air = rowMeans(cbind(norm_no2, norm_pm25), na.rm = TRUE),
                        norm_air = ifelse(is.nan(norm_air), NA_real_, norm_air))
k_vars <- c("norm_lst", "norm_dist_bs", "norm_air", "norm_green_time", "norm_traffic_cat", "norm_income_weighted")
k_lab  <- c("Urban heat", "Blue space", "Air quality", "Green proximity", "Traffic", "Low income")
k_w <- c(k_w7[c("norm_lst", "norm_dist_bs")], norm_air = unname(k_w7["norm_no2"] + k_w7["norm_pm25"]),
         k_w7[c("norm_green_time", "norm_traffic_cat", "norm_income_weighted")])[k_vars]

shared <- list(Malta      = c("norm_lst", "norm_no2", "norm_traffic", "norm_green_time", "norm_dist_bs"),
               Klagenfurt = c("norm_lst", "norm_air", "norm_traffic_cat", "norm_green_time", "norm_dist_bs"))

cities <- list(
  Malta = list(df = malta, id = "gid", vars = m_vars, lab = setNames(m_lab, m_vars), w = m_w,
               pop = "Total_Population", border = readRDS(here::here("data/malta/malta_union_boundary.rds"))),
  Klagenfurt = list(df = klag, id = "ID", vars = k_vars, lab = setNames(k_lab, k_vars), w = k_w,
                    pop = "popdense_2020", border = readRDS(here::here("data/klagenfurt/klagenfurt_boundary.rds"))))

weights_tab <- bind_rows(
  tibble(city = "Malta", criterion = m_lab, variable = m_vars, citizen_pct = 100 * m_w, equal_pct = 100 / length(m_vars)),
  tibble(city = "Klagenfurt", criterion = k_lab, variable = k_vars, citizen_pct = 100 * k_w, equal_pct = 100 / length(k_vars)))
ktab(weights_tab, "Citizen and equal weights at criterion level (%)", 1)
```

```{r helpers}
# Weighted mean over available criteria, for a matrix of weight sets (criteria x sets)
score_mat <- function(S, W) {
  A <- !is.na(S); S0 <- S; S0[!A] <- 0
  (S0 %*% W) / (A %*% W)
}
top5 <- function(x) dplyr::ntile(x, 5) == 5
cmp <- function(x, ref) {
  qx <- dplyr::ntile(x, 5); qr <- dplyr::ntile(ref, 5)
  c(spearman = cor(x, ref, method = "spearman"),
    top_quintile_overlap_pct = 100 * mean(qx[qr == 5] == 5),
    cells_changing_quintile_pct = 100 * mean(qx != qr))
}
rdirichlet1 <- function(n, k) { g <- matrix(rexp(n * k), nrow = k); sweep(g, 2, colSums(g), "/") }
```

## Preparation

For each city: the scored cells, the criteria matrix, the citizen and equal weights scores, and the
`r N_DRAWS` random weight sets (all criteria and five shared criteria). Everything below reuses these.

```{r prep}
P <- list()
for (cn in names(cities)) {
  ci <- cities[[cn]]
  d  <- ci$df %>% filter(scored)
  S  <- as.matrix(st_drop_geometry(d)[, ci$vars])
  k  <- length(ci$vars)
  w_eq <- rep(1 / k, k)
  sv <- shared[[cn]]; S5 <- S[, sv]
  w5c <- ci$w[sv] / sum(ci$w[sv])
  set.seed(SEED); W  <- rdirichlet1(N_DRAWS, k)
  set.seed(SEED); W5 <- rdirichlet1(N_DRAWS, 5)
  P[[cn]] <- list(d = d, S = S, k = k, w_eq = w_eq, S5 = S5, w5c = w5c, W = W, W5 = W5,
                  s_cit  = as.numeric(score_mat(S, matrix(ci$w, ncol = 1))),
                  s_eq   = as.numeric(score_mat(S, matrix(w_eq, ncol = 1))),
                  s_cit5 = as.numeric(score_mat(S5, matrix(w5c, ncol = 1))),
                  s_eq5  = as.numeric(score_mat(S5, matrix(rep(1 / 5, 5), ncol = 1))),
                  SC  = score_mat(S, W), SC5 = score_mat(S5, W5))
}
check <- bind_rows(lapply(names(P), function(cn) tibble(
  city = cn, scored_cells = nrow(P[[cn]]$d), criteria = P[[cn]]$k,
  max_abs_diff_vs_saved = max(abs(P[[cn]]$s_cit - P[[cn]]$d$priority_citizen)),
  spearman_vs_saved = cor(P[[cn]]$s_cit, P[[cn]]$d$priority_citizen, method = "spearman"))))
stopifnot(all(check$spearman_vs_saved > 0.9999))
ktab(check, "Check: the criterion level citizen score reproduces the saved priority_citizen", 6)
```

# A. Burden coincidence

All on the scored cells. If burdens coincide, the criteria are positively correlated, the first principal
component carries a large share of the variance, and more cells than chance are in the top quintile of
several criteria at once.

## Step 1. Correlation between criteria

```{r A1-correlation}
cor_mats <- lapply(names(cities), function(cn) {
  cm <- cor(P[[cn]]$S, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  dimnames(cm) <- list(cities[[cn]]$lab[cities[[cn]]$vars], cities[[cn]]$lab[cities[[cn]]$vars]); cm
}) %>% setNames(names(cities))
A1 <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cor_mats), function(cn) {
  off <- cor_mats[[cn]][upper.tri(cor_mats[[cn]])]
  tibble(city = cn, pairs = length(off), mean_abs_spearman = mean(abs(off)), mean_spearman = mean(off),
         positive_pairs = sum(off > 0), pairs_above_0.3 = sum(off > 0.3), pairs_below_minus_0.3 = sum(off < -0.3),
         min_spearman = min(off), max_spearman = max(off))
}))
ktab(A1, "A1. Spearman correlations between criteria (pairs of criteria)")
```

```{r A1-heatmaps, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5}
heat <- function(cn) {
  m <- cor_mats[[cn]]
  df <- as.data.frame(as.table(m)) %>%
    mutate(Var1 = factor(Var1, levels = rownames(m)), Var2 = factor(Var2, levels = rev(rownames(m))))
  ggplot(df, aes(Var1, Var2, fill = Freq)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Freq)), size = 2.6) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b", limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Spearman") +
    labs(title = cn, x = NULL, y = NULL) + coord_equal() +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), panel.grid = element_blank())
}
heat("Malta") + heat("Klagenfurt") + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

## Step 2. Principal components

PC1 from the eigenvalues of the pairwise Spearman matrix (all scored cells). The PCA on complete cases is
shown alongside: in Malta it keeps fewer than half of the cells, because green per person is missing in
unpopulated cells. "If independent" is the share PC1 would have if the criteria were uncorrelated (1 / number
of criteria).

```{r A2-pca}
A2 <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) {
  ev_s <- eigen(cor_mats[[cn]], symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  cc <- complete.cases(P[[cn]]$S); ev_c <- prcomp(P[[cn]]$S[cc, ], scale. = TRUE)$sdev^2
  tibble(city = cn, criteria = P[[cn]]$k, pc1_variance_pct = 100 * ev_s[1] / sum(ev_s), pc1_eigenvalue = ev_s[1],
         pc1_pct_if_independent = 100 / P[[cn]]$k,
         pca_complete_cases = sum(cc), pc1_variance_pct_complete_cases = 100 * ev_c[1] / sum(ev_c))
}))
ktab(A2, "A2. Variance explained by the first principal component")
```

```{r A2-scree, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.5}
bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) {
  ev <- eigen(cor_mats[[cn]], symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  tibble(city = cn, component = seq_along(ev), variance_pct = 100 * ev / sum(ev))
})) %>%
  ggplot(aes(component, variance_pct, colour = city)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = city_cols, name = NULL) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(x = "Principal component", y = "Variance explained (%)") + theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

PC1 loadings: the correlation of each criterion with the first component. The sign of an eigenvector is
arbitrary, so it is set to make the sum of loadings positive.

```{r A2-loadings}
load_pc1 <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) {
  e <- eigen(cor_mats[[cn]], symmetric = TRUE)
  v <- e$vectors[, 1] * sign(sum(e$vectors[, 1]))
  tibble(city      = cn,
         criterion = colnames(cor_mats[[cn]]),
         loading   = v * sqrt(e$values[1]))   # correlación de cada criterio con la PC1
})) %>% arrange(city, desc(abs(loading)))
ktab(load_pc1, "PC1 loadings")
```

## Step 3. Cells in the top quintile of several criteria

**Main rule (decided 25 November 2026).** For each criterion, over the cells where it is defined
(scored and not missing), cells are ranked by burden (highest priority first). Cells strictly above the
value that contains the 20% boundary have membership 1; cells at the boundary value (the boundary class
for a categorical criterion, or the tie) have membership f = (0.20 minus the share strictly above) / the
share at the boundary value; all other cells have membership 0. Cells with a criterion score of 0 (no
burden) never get membership: if the 20% boundary falls in the zero class, the criterion keeps only the
cells above it (f = 0; Klagenfurt traffic, 13.6%). Every other criterion has exactly 20% membership. For a
continuous criterion without ties at the boundary this is the same as before.

Memberships are treated as independent probabilities within a cell, so each cell has a probability of
being in the top quintile of 0, 1, 2, ... criteria (Poisson binomial). The observed number of cells in the
top quintile of three or more criteria is the sum of these probabilities over cells. The comparison is with
the same quantity after shuffling each criterion's memberships only among the cells where that criterion is
defined (`r N_PERM` shuffles, seed `r SEED`), because the two cities have different numbers of criteria and
some criteria are missing in part of the cells (Malta green per person and Klagenfurt low income in
unpopulated cells).

**Sensitivity rows.** Old tie rule: top class = at or above p80 among cells with a value; where ties make
that class larger than 25%, strictly above p80. Old shuffle: across all scored cells, including the cells
where the criterion is missing. The old tie rule with the old shuffle is the result reported up to 24
November 2026.

### Step 3a. Tie rule per criterion

```{r A3a-tierule}
# Old rule: at or above p80; strictly above p80 if that class is larger than 25% of cells with a value
old_top <- function(x) {
  q <- quantile(x, 0.8, na.rm = TRUE); t <- !is.na(x) & x >= q
  if (mean(t[!is.na(x)]) > 0.25) t <- !is.na(x) & x > q
  as.numeric(t)
}
# New rule: fractional membership at the value that contains the 20% boundary (exactly 20% per criterion),
# except that cells with score 0 (no burden) never count: a boundary in the zero class gives f = 0
frac_top <- function(x, p = 0.2) {
  d <- !is.na(x); n <- sum(d); xs <- x[d]
  v <- sort(unique(xs), decreasing = TRUE)
  idx <- match(xs, v); cnt <- tabulate(idx, nbins = length(v))
  above <- c(0, cumsum(cnt))[seq_along(v)] / n        # share strictly above each value
  b <- which(above + cnt / n >= p - 1e-12)[1]          # value that contains the boundary
  f <- (p - above[b]) / (cnt[b] / n)
  if (v[b] == 0) f <- 0                                # score 0 = no burden, never a member
  m <- numeric(length(x)); m[d] <- ifelse(idx < b, 1, ifelse(idx == b, f, 0))
  list(m = m, info = tibble(n_defined = n, boundary_value = v[b], share_above_pct = 100 * above[b],
                            share_boundary_pct = 100 * cnt[b] / n, f = f))
}

memb <- list(); tie_tab <- list()
for (cn in names(cities)) {
  S <- P[[cn]]$S
  fr <- lapply(seq_len(ncol(S)), function(j) frac_top(S[, j]))
  M_new <- sapply(fr, `[[`, "m"); M_old <- apply(S, 2, old_top)
  colnames(M_new) <- colnames(M_old) <- colnames(S)
  def <- !is.na(S)
  zero_b <- sapply(fr, function(z) z$info$boundary_value == 0)
  stopifnot(all(abs(colSums(M_new)[!zero_b] / colSums(def)[!zero_b] - 0.2) < 1e-9),
            all(colSums(M_new)[zero_b] / colSums(def)[zero_b] < 0.2),
            all(M_new[!def] == 0), all(M_old[!def] == 0), all(M_new[!is.na(S) & S == 0] == 0))
  memb[[cn]] <- list(old = M_old, new = M_new, defined = def)
  tie_tab[[cn]] <- bind_rows(lapply(fr, `[[`, "info")) %>%
    mutate(city = cn, criterion = cities[[cn]]$lab[colnames(S)], .before = 1) %>%
    mutate(defined_pct_of_scored = 100 * n_defined / nrow(S),
           old_share_pct = 100 * colSums(M_old) / n_defined,
           new_share_pct = 100 * colSums(M_new) / n_defined,
           cells_fractional = colSums(M_new > 0 & M_new < 1))
}
tie_tab <- bind_rows(tie_tab)
ktab(tie_tab %>% select(city, criterion, n_defined, defined_pct_of_scored, share_above_pct, share_boundary_pct, f,
                        old_share_pct, new_share_pct, cells_fractional),
     "A3a. Tie rule per criterion: share strictly above the boundary value, share at the boundary value, f, old top class share (25% fallback) and new share (% of cells where the criterion is defined)", 3)
```

```{r A3a-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
last_plot_A3a <- tie_tab %>%
  select(city, criterion, old_share_pct, new_share_pct, f) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(old_share_pct, new_share_pct), names_to = "rule", values_to = "share") %>%
  mutate(rule = recode(rule, old_share_pct = "Old tie rule (25% fallback)", new_share_pct = "New tie rule (fractional)")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(share, reorder(criterion, share), colour = rule)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 20, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) + facet_wrap(~ city, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`Old tie rule (25% fallback)` = "grey55", `New tie rule (fractional)` = "black"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Top quintile membership (% of cells where the criterion is defined)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
last_plot_A3a
```

### Step 3b. Three or more burdens: observed vs shuffled, four combinations

```{r A3b-variants}
# Poisson binomial distribution of the number of top quintile memberships per cell (cells x 0..k)
pb_dist <- function(M) {
  k <- ncol(M); D <- matrix(0, nrow(M), k + 1); D[, 1] <- 1
  for (j in seq_len(k)) {
    p <- M[, j]
    D[, 2:(k + 1)] <- D[, 2:(k + 1)] * (1 - p) + D[, 1:k] * p
    D[, 1] <- D[, 1] * (1 - p)
  }
  D
}
# Shuffle each criterion: across all scored cells (old) or only among cells where it is defined (restricted)
shuffle_M <- function(M, def, restricted) {
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(M))) {
    if (restricted) { i <- which(def[, j]); M[i, j] <- M[i, j][sample.int(length(i))] }
    else M[, j] <- M[sample.int(nrow(M)), j]
  }
  M
}
variants <- tibble(tie_rule = c("old", "new", "old", "new"), shuffle = c("all", "all", "restricted", "restricted"),
                   label = c("Old tie rule + old shuffle (reported to 24 Nov)", "New tie rule + old shuffle",
                             "Old tie rule + restricted shuffle", "New tie rule + restricted shuffle (main)"))

dist_l <- list(); A3v <- list()
for (cn in names(cities)) {
  def <- memb[[cn]]$defined; n <- nrow(def); k <- ncol(def)
  for (v in seq_len(nrow(variants))) {
    M <- memb[[cn]][[variants$tie_rule[v]]]
    obs <- colSums(pb_dist(M))
    set.seed(SEED)
    perm <- replicate(N_PERM, colSums(pb_dist(shuffle_M(M, def, variants$shuffle[v] == "restricted"))))
    o3 <- sum(obs[4:(k + 1)]); p3 <- colSums(perm[4:(k + 1), , drop = FALSE])
    A3v[[length(A3v) + 1]] <- tibble(
      city = cn, variant = variants$label[v], tie_rule = variants$tie_rule[v], shuffle = variants$shuffle[v],
      observed_cells = o3, observed_pct = 100 * o3 / n,
      shuffled_mean_pct = 100 * mean(p3) / n, shuffled_p5_pct = 100 * quantile(p3, 0.05, names = FALSE) / n,
      shuffled_p95_pct = 100 * quantile(p3, 0.95, names = FALSE) / n,
      ratio = o3 / mean(p3), ratio_p5 = o3 / quantile(p3, 0.95, names = FALSE),
      ratio_p95 = o3 / quantile(p3, 0.05, names = FALSE))
    dist_l[[length(dist_l) + 1]] <- tibble(city = cn, variant = variants$label[v], n_top_criteria = 0:k,
                                           observed_pct = 100 * obs / n, permuted_pct = 100 * rowMeans(perm) / n)
  }
}
A3v <- bind_rows(A3v) %>% mutate(variant = factor(variant, levels = variants$label))
dist_all <- bind_rows(dist_l)
ktab(A3v %>% transmute(city, variant, observed_cells, observed_pct,
                       shuffled = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", shuffled_mean_pct, shuffled_p5_pct, shuffled_p95_pct),
                       ratio, ratio_interval = sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", ratio_p5, ratio_p95)),
     "A3b. Cells in the top quintile of three or more criteria (% of scored cells): observed, shuffled mean (5th to 95th percentile) and ratio observed / shuffled mean; ratio interval = observed / shuffled 95th to 5th percentile", 3)
```

```{r A3b-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.8}
last_plot_A3b <- A3v %>%
  mutate(main = grepl("main", variant)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ratio, forcats::fct_rev(variant), colour = city, shape = main)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ratio_p5, xmax = ratio_p95), height = 0.2) + geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ city) + scale_colour_manual(values = city_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Ratio observed / shuffled, cells in the top quintile of 3+ criteria\n(interval from the 5th to 95th shuffle percentile)",
       y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
last_plot_A3b
```

### Step 3c. Distribution, main result

```{r A3c-main}
MAIN_A3 <- "New tie rule + restricted shuffle (main)"
dist_top <- dist_all %>% filter(variant == MAIN_A3) %>% select(-variant)
ktab(dist_top %>% filter(n_top_criteria <= 6),
     "A3c. Cells by number of criteria in which they are in the top quintile, main result (expected %; 7 or more not shown)", 1)

A3 <- A3v %>% filter(variant == MAIN_A3) %>%
  transmute(city, top_quintile_3plus_pct = observed_pct, top_quintile_3plus_pct_permuted = shuffled_mean_pct,
            ratio_to_permuted = ratio)
ktab(A3, "A3d. Share of scored cells in the top quintile of three or more criteria, main result (%)")
```

```{r A3-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
dist_top %>% pivot_longer(c(observed_pct, permuted_pct), names_to = "what", values_to = "pct") %>%
  mutate(what = recode(what, observed_pct = "Observed", permuted_pct = "Shuffled (chance)")) %>%
  filter(n_top_criteria <= 6) %>%
  ggplot(aes(n_top_criteria, pct, fill = what)) + geom_col(position = "dodge") + facet_wrap(~ city) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Observed = "grey30", `Shuffled (chance)` = "grey75"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Number of criteria with the cell in their top quintile (expected)", y = "Cells (%)") + theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

```{r A-summary}
A <- A1 %>% left_join(A2, by = "city") %>% left_join(A3, by = "city")
ktab(A %>% select(city, mean_abs_spearman, mean_spearman, pc1_variance_pct, pc1_pct_if_independent,
                  top_quintile_3plus_pct, top_quintile_3plus_pct_permuted, ratio_to_permuted),
     "A. Summary")
```

# B. Sensitivity to weights in general

`r N_DRAWS` weight sets per city, Dirichlet(1, ..., 1), seed `r SEED`. Each random score is compared with
the equal weights score on the same cells: Spearman and the share of the equal weights top quintile that
stays in the top quintile.

```{r B-draws}
draws_B <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) {
  st <- t(apply(P[[cn]]$SC, 2, cmp, ref = P[[cn]]$s_eq))
  tibble(city = cn, set = "All criteria", draw = seq_len(N_DRAWS),
         dist_from_equal = sqrt(colSums((P[[cn]]$W - P[[cn]]$w_eq)^2)),
         spearman = st[, "spearman"], top_quintile_overlap_pct = st[, "top_quintile_overlap_pct"])
}))
summ_draws <- function(dd) dd %>% group_by(city, set) %>%
  summarise(spearman_median = median(spearman), spearman_p05 = quantile(spearman, 0.05),
            spearman_p95 = quantile(spearman, 0.95), overlap_median = median(top_quintile_overlap_pct),
            overlap_p05 = quantile(top_quintile_overlap_pct, 0.05), overlap_p95 = quantile(top_quintile_overlap_pct, 0.95),
            dist_from_equal_median = median(dist_from_equal), .groups = "drop")
B_all <- summ_draws(draws_B)
ktab(B_all %>% select(-set), "B. Random weights vs equal weights: median and 5th to 95th percentile")
```

Citizen weights value against the random draws: the percentile is the share of the `r N_DRAWS` random
weight sets whose agreement with the equal weights map is strictly lower than the citizen weights value
(ties reported separately).

```{r B-citizen}
# Citizen weights vs equal weights, same comparison as the random draws
cit_vs_eq <- function(set, s_c, s_e) bind_rows(lapply(names(P), function(cn) {
  ce <- cmp(s_c(cn), s_e(cn))
  tibble(city = cn, set = set, spearman = ce[["spearman"]], top_quintile_overlap_pct = ce[["top_quintile_overlap_pct"]])
}))
# Percentile of the citizen value within the random draws
cit_pct <- function(dd, cit) cit %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(
  spearman_pct_below  = 100 * mean(dd$spearman[dd$city == city & dd$set == set] < spearman),
  spearman_pct_tied   = 100 * mean(dd$spearman[dd$city == city & dd$set == set] == spearman),
  overlap_pct_below   = 100 * mean(dd$top_quintile_overlap_pct[dd$city == city & dd$set == set] < top_quintile_overlap_pct),
  overlap_pct_tied    = 100 * mean(dd$top_quintile_overlap_pct[dd$city == city & dd$set == set] == top_quintile_overlap_pct)) %>%
  ungroup()
cit_B <- cit_vs_eq("All criteria", function(cn) P[[cn]]$s_cit, function(cn) P[[cn]]$s_eq) %>% cit_pct(draws_B, .)
ktab(cit_B, "B. Citizen weights vs equal weights, and the % of random weight sets with lower agreement", 3)
```

```{r B-hist-fun}
source(here::here("R/theme_lancet.R"))
# One histogram per city (Klagenfurt above, Malta below), same x axis; dashed line = median of the
# random draws, solid line = citizen weights
hist_draws <- function(dd, cit, y, binwidth, xlab, fmt) {
  dd  <- dd %>% mutate(city = factor(city, levels = c("Klagenfurt", "Malta")))
  cit <- cit %>% mutate(city = factor(city, levels = c("Klagenfurt", "Malta")))
  med <- dd %>% group_by(city) %>% summarise(v = median(.data[[y]]), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(lab = paste0("Median ", fmt(v)))
  cv  <- cit %>% transmute(city, v = .data[[y]], lab = paste0("Citizen weights ", fmt(v)))
  rng <- range(c(dd[[y]], cv$v))
  ggplot(dd, aes(.data[[y]], fill = city)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = binwidth, boundary = 0, colour = NA) +
    geom_vline(data = med, aes(xintercept = v), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_vline(data = cv, aes(xintercept = v), linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_label(data = med, aes(v, Inf, label = lab), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.5,
               size = pt_size(7), family = lancet_font, fill = "white", label.size = 0,
               label.padding = unit(0.5, "mm")) +
    geom_label(data = cv, aes(v, Inf, label = lab), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 1.05, vjust = 3.2,
               size = pt_size(7), family = lancet_font, fill = "white", label.size = 0,
               label.padding = unit(0.5, "mm")) +
    facet_wrap(~ city, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = city_cols, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(floor(rng[1] / binwidth) * binwidth, ceiling(rng[2] / binwidth) * binwidth + binwidth)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.35))) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = "Number of random weight sets (of 1,000)") +
    theme_lancet() + theme(plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 3, 3))
}
X_SP <- "Agreement with the equal weights map (Spearman)"
X_OV <- "Top quintile cells shared with the equal weights map (%)"
f_sp <- function(v) sprintf("%.3f", v)
f_ov <- function(v) sprintf("%.1f%%", v)
```

```{r B-plot, fig.width=180/25.4, fig.height=110/25.4}
pB_sp <- hist_draws(draws_B, cit_B, "spearman", 0.01, X_SP, f_sp)
pB_ov <- hist_draws(draws_B, cit_B, "top_quintile_overlap_pct", 1, X_OV, f_ov)
pB_sp
pB_ov
```

# C. Controls

## C1. Five shared criteria

The same `r N_DRAWS` draws, using only urban heat, air quality, traffic, green proximity and blue space,
with equal weight 1/5 in both cities. This removes the difference in the number and type of criteria. If
Klagenfurt is still more stable, the difference comes from how the burdens are arranged in space, not from
how many criteria each city has.

### Step 1. Which criteria

```{r C1-criteria}
bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) tibble(
  city = cn, criterion = cities[[cn]]$lab[shared[[cn]]], variable = shared[[cn]],
  citizen_weight_rescaled_pct = 100 * P[[cn]]$w5c))) %>%
  ktab("C1a. The five shared criteria and their citizen weights, rescaled to sum to 100%", 1)
```

### Step 2. Correlation among the five shared criteria

```{r C1-correlation}
bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) {
  cm <- cor(P[[cn]]$S5, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"); off <- cm[upper.tri(cm)]
  tibble(city = cn, mean_abs_spearman = mean(abs(off)), mean_spearman = mean(off), positive_pairs = sum(off > 0))
})) %>% ktab("C1b. Spearman correlations among the five shared criteria (10 pairs)")
```

### Step 3. Random weights on the five shared criteria

```{r C1-draws}
draws_C1 <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) {
  st <- t(apply(P[[cn]]$SC5, 2, cmp, ref = P[[cn]]$s_eq5))
  tibble(city = cn, set = "Five shared criteria", draw = seq_len(N_DRAWS),
         dist_from_equal = sqrt(colSums((P[[cn]]$W5 - 1 / 5)^2)),
         spearman = st[, "spearman"], top_quintile_overlap_pct = st[, "top_quintile_overlap_pct"])
}))
B_C1 <- summ_draws(draws_C1)
ktab(B_C1 %>% select(-set), "C1c. Five shared criteria: random vs equal weights, median and 5th to 95th percentile")
```

### Step 4. All criteria vs five shared criteria

```{r C1-compare}
bind_rows(B_all, B_C1) %>% select(city, set, spearman_median, spearman_p05, spearman_p95, overlap_median) %>%
  arrange(city, set) %>% ktab("C1d. Random weights: all criteria (B) vs five shared criteria (C1)")
draws <- bind_rows(draws_B, draws_C1)
```

```{r C1-citizen}
cit_C1 <- cit_vs_eq("Five shared criteria", function(cn) P[[cn]]$s_cit5, function(cn) P[[cn]]$s_eq5) %>%
  cit_pct(draws_C1, .)
ktab(cit_C1, "C1e. Five shared criteria: citizen weights vs equal weights, and the % of random weight sets with lower agreement", 3)
```

```{r C1-plot, fig.width=180/25.4, fig.height=110/25.4}
pC1_sp <- hist_draws(draws_C1, cit_C1, "spearman", 0.01, X_SP, f_sp)
pC1_ov <- hist_draws(draws_C1, cit_C1, "top_quintile_overlap_pct", 1, X_OV, f_ov)
pC1_sp
pC1_ov
```

## C2. Map change per unit of weight change

Citizen weights move each city away from equal weights by some amount (the Euclidean distance between
the two weight vectors). C2 asks how much the map changes for that amount of weight change.

### Step 1. How far citizen weights are from equal weights

```{r C2-weights}
w_gap <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) tibble(
  city = cn, criterion = cities[[cn]]$lab[cities[[cn]]$vars], citizen_pct = 100 * cities[[cn]]$w,
  equal_pct = 100 * P[[cn]]$w_eq, difference_pct_points = 100 * (cities[[cn]]$w - P[[cn]]$w_eq))))
ktab(w_gap, "C2a. Citizen minus equal weight per criterion (percentage points)", 1)
```

### Step 2. Distance and map change, citizen vs equal

```{r C2-change}
c2_row <- function(cn, set, s_c, s_e, wc, we) {
  ce <- cmp(s_c, s_e); dce <- sqrt(sum((wc - we)^2))
  tibble(city = cn, set = set, dist_citizen_equal = dce, spearman = ce[["spearman"]],
         one_minus_spearman = 1 - ce[["spearman"]], top_quintile_overlap_pct = ce[["top_quintile_overlap_pct"]],
         change_per_unit_weight = (1 - ce[["spearman"]]) / dce)
}
C2 <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) bind_rows(
  c2_row(cn, "All criteria", P[[cn]]$s_cit, P[[cn]]$s_eq, cities[[cn]]$w, P[[cn]]$w_eq),
  c2_row(cn, "Five shared criteria", P[[cn]]$s_cit5, P[[cn]]$s_eq5, P[[cn]]$w5c, rep(1 / 5, 5)))))
ktab(C2, "C2b. Citizen vs equal weights: weight distance and map change")
```

### Step 3. The same relation across the random draws

Slope of 1 − Spearman on the distance from equal weights across the `r N_DRAWS` draws (regression through
the origin): the city's general map change per unit of weight change, against which the citizen weights
(diamonds) can be read.

```{r C2-slope}
C2 <- C2 %>% left_join(draws %>% group_by(city, set) %>%
  summarise(random_draws_slope = unname(coef(lm(I(1 - spearman) ~ 0 + dist_from_equal))[1]), .groups = "drop"),
  by = c("city", "set"))
ktab(C2 %>% select(city, set, change_per_unit_weight, random_draws_slope),
     "C2c. Map change per unit of weight distance: citizen weights and random draws")
```

```{r C2-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
pC <- ggplot(draws, aes(dist_from_equal, 1 - spearman, colour = city)) + geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_abline(data = C2, aes(slope = random_draws_slope, intercept = 0, colour = city), linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(data = C2, aes(dist_citizen_equal, one_minus_spearman, fill = city), shape = 23, size = 3, colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ set, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = city_cols, name = NULL) + scale_fill_manual(values = city_cols, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Euclidean distance of the weight vector from equal weights", y = "1 - Spearman vs equal weights",
       caption = "Points: random weight sets. Dashed: slope through the origin. Diamonds: citizen weights.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
pC
```

# D. Robust and contested cells

## Step 1. How often each cell is in the top quintile

Share of the `r N_DRAWS` draws in which each scored cell is in the top quintile.

```{r D1-ptop}
for (cn in names(cities)) P[[cn]]$p_top <- rowMeans(apply(P[[cn]]$SC, 2, top5))
bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) tibble(city = cn, p = 100 * P[[cn]]$p_top))) %>%
  group_by(city) %>%
  summarise(never_pct = 100 * mean(p == 0), always_pct = 100 * mean(p == 100),
            median = median(p), p25 = quantile(p, 0.25), p75 = quantile(p, 0.75), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ktab("D1. Draws with the cell in the top quintile (%): share of cells never and always, and quartiles", 1)
```

```{r D1-hist, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) tibble(city = cn, p_top = P[[cn]]$p_top))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(100 * p_top, fill = city)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 2.5, boundary = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(10, 90), linetype = 2) + facet_wrap(~ city, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = city_cols, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Draws with the cell in the top quintile (%)", y = "Cells") + theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

## Step 2. Classes: cells and residents

Robust core: over 90% of draws. Contested: 10% to 90%. Rarely prioritised: under 10%. Residents: Malta
`pop_reallocated_nso` (`Total_Population`), Klagenfurt GHSL 2020 (`popdense_2020`).

```{r D2-classes}
cls_levels <- c("Rarely prioritised (< 10%)", "Contested (10% to 90%)", "Robust core (> 90%)")
cells_D <- list()
for (cn in names(cities)) {
  p <- P[[cn]]$p_top
  cls <- factor(case_when(p > 0.90 ~ cls_levels[3], p >= 0.10 ~ cls_levels[2], TRUE ~ cls_levels[1]), levels = cls_levels)
  cells_D[[cn]] <- P[[cn]]$d %>% mutate(p_top = p, robust_class = cls, citizen_top = top5(P[[cn]]$s_cit)) %>%
    select(all_of(cities[[cn]]$id), all_of(cities[[cn]]$pop), p_top, robust_class, citizen_top)
}
D <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) {
  dd <- st_drop_geometry(cells_D[[cn]]); pop <- dd[[cities[[cn]]$pop]]; pop[is.na(pop)] <- 0
  tibble(city = cn, class = dd$robust_class, pop = pop) %>% group_by(city, class, .drop = FALSE) %>%
    summarise(cells = n(), residents = sum(pop), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(cells_pct = 100 * cells / sum(cells), residents_pct = 100 * residents / sum(residents))
}))
ktab(D, "D2. Robust and contested cells: cells and residents per class", 1)
```

```{r D2-maps, fig.width=12, fig.height=6.5}
dmap <- function(cn) {
  ci <- cities[[cn]]; d <- cells_D[[cn]]
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = st_transform(ci$df, st_crs(d)), fill = "grey92", colour = NA) +
    geom_sf(data = d, aes(fill = robust_class), colour = NA) +
    geom_sf(data = st_transform(ci$border, st_crs(d)), fill = NA, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Rarely prioritised (< 10%)" = "#d9e6f2", "Contested (10% to 90%)" = "#f4a582",
                                 "Robust core (> 90%)" = "#b2182b"), name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    labs(title = cn) + theme_void(base_size = 10)
}
pD <- dmap("Malta") + dmap("Klagenfurt") + plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
pD
```

<!-- TODO: update text (2026-11-25): unscored cells now also include water cells in both cities (spec 1.3). -->
Grey cells are not scored (in Malta, mainly the airport and port).

## Step 3. Classes and the citizen top quintile

How the classes relate to the actual citizen weighted map: where do the citizen top quintile cells fall?

```{r D3-citizen}
bind_rows(lapply(names(cities), function(cn) st_drop_geometry(cells_D[[cn]]) %>%
  filter(citizen_top) %>% count(robust_class, .drop = FALSE, name = "citizen_top_quintile_cells") %>%
  mutate(pct_of_citizen_top_quintile = 100 * citizen_top_quintile_cells / sum(citizen_top_quintile_cells)) %>%
  mutate(city = cn, .before = 1))) %>%
  ktab("D3. Citizen top quintile cells by robustness class", 1)
```

# Leave one out and sensitivity summary (Table S6)

Computed in the scoring notebooks (`Malta_MCDA_260702_realloc.Rmd`, `Klagenfurt_MCDA_260520.Rmd`) against the main citizen score. The "without ..." rows are the leave one out analysis: each criterion dropped in turn and the other weights rescaled to sum to 1. In Klagenfurt, air quality drops NO2 and PM2.5 together. The Klagenfurt "citizen vs equal weights" row uses the notebook's equal weights, 1/7 per indicator (air quality 2/7), not 1/6 per criterion as in A to D.
<!-- TODO: update text. Since 2026-11-25 the Klagenfurt scoring notebook uses 1/6 per criterion (air quality 1/12 NO2 + 1/12 PM2.5), the same as A to D. -->


```{r s6}
s6 <- bind_rows(readRDS(here::here("data/malta/malta_sensitivity.rds")) %>% mutate(city = "Malta", .before = 1),
                readRDS(here::here("data/klagenfurt/klag_sensitivity.rds")) %>% mutate(city = "Klagenfurt", .before = 1))
s6_tab <- s6 %>% rename(`Sensitivity test` = test_name, Spearman = spearman_r, `Top quintile retained` = class_agreement,
                        `Cells changing quintile` = cells_changing_quintile)
s6_cap <- "Sensitivity summary, both cities (main score vs each variant, cells scored in both)"
if (knitting()) {
  s6_tab %>% kable(caption = s6_cap) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
    collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top")
} else ktab(s6_tab, s6_cap)
```

```{r loo-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
s6 %>% filter(grepl("^Without", test_name)) %>%
  mutate(spearman = as.numeric(spearman_r), criterion = sub("^Without ", "", test_name)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(reorder(criterion, spearman), spearman, fill = city)) + geom_col() + coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ city, scales = "free_y") + scale_fill_manual(values = city_cols, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Spearman, main score vs score without the criterion") + theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```
